EcoBuilder (Component-by-Component API)¶

EcoBuilder builds a pre-sized DHWSystem from components the caller defines: temperatures, tank volumes, recirc loop, performance maps, controls and water heaters. No sizing is done, and the system’s get_minimum_*() getters raise RuntimeError.

Use it when each heater needs its own controls or schedule, which the flat parameter set of EcosizerEngine does not allow. Simulate the result with simulate_3day() or simulate_annual().

EcoBuilder is re-exported from the top-level ecoengine package.

__init__(perf_map_dir: str | None = None, climate_data_dir: str | None = None) → None[source]¶
Parameters:

  • perf_map_dir (str, optional) – Directory with maps.json and pkls/ used by build_performance_map(). Defaults to the bundled data.

  • climate_data_dir (str, optional) – Climate data directory used by build_building(). Defaults to the bundled data.

define_temperatures(supply_temp_f: float | None = None, storage_temp_f: float | None = None) → None[source]¶

Set (or overwrite) the supply and/or storage temperature [°F].

define_storage_volume(gal: float, storage_type: str = 'primary', drawdown_fract: float | None = None, supply_temp_f: float | None = None) → None[source]¶

Set (or overwrite) a tank volume.

Parameters:

  • gal (float) – Tank volume [gal]. Must be > 0.

  • storage_type (str) – 'primary', 'tm' or 'in_series'.

  • drawdown_fract (float, optional) – 'primary' only: fraction of the tank above the cold-water inlet (0 < drawdown_fract <= 1). Only used by multi-pass RTP schematics.

  • supply_temp_f (float, optional) – Also sets (or overwrites) the supply temperature [°F].

Raises:

ValueError – On an unknown storage_type, a non-positive volume, or an invalid drawdown_fract.

define_recirc(return_temp_f: float, return_flow_gpm: float, supply_temp_f: float | None = None) → None[source]¶

Set (or overwrite) the recirc loop return temperature [°F] and flow [GPM], and optionally the supply temperature [°F].

build_performance_map(model_name: str | None = None, nominal_capacity_kbtuh: float | None = None, num_units: int = 1, design_inlet_temp_f: float = 50.0) → PerformanceMap[source]¶

Build a PerformanceMap for use in build_water_heater().

Parameters:

  • model_name (str, optional) – Model name from maps.json. When given, the map is loaded from the registry and nominal_capacity_kbtuh (total, all units) is only used as the electric-resistance fallback below the map’s minimum OAT.

  • nominal_capacity_kbtuh (float, optional) – Without model_name: the constant total capacity [kBTU/hr] of a NominalPerformanceMap.

  • num_units (int) – Number of identical units (model maps only). Default 1.

  • design_inlet_temp_f (float) – Fallback inlet temperature for model maps [°F]. Default 50.

Raises:

ValueError – If neither model_name nor nominal_capacity_kbtuh is given, or num_units != 1 without model_name.

build_control_setting(on_sensor_fract: float | None, on_trigger_t_f: float | None, off_sensor_fract: float | None, off_trigger_t_f: float | None, outlet_temp_f: float) → Controls[source]¶

Build a Controls object for one operating mode of a control map.

If the four sensor/trigger values are all None, returns an AlwaysOffControls (heater never fires in that mode).

Raises:

ValueError – If only some of the four sensor/trigger values are None.

build_control_schedule(start_times: list[list] | None = None) → list[str][source]¶

Build a 24-hour control schedule from mode start hours.

Each mode runs from its start hour until the next mode’s start hour (or the end of the day).

Parameters:

start_times (list[[str, int]], optional) –

[mode, start_hour] pairs, in any order. One must start at hour 0. None → ['normal'] * 24.

[['normal', 0], ['shed', 12], ['normal', 18]] → normal except hours 12–17 shed.

Raises:

ValueError – If no mode starts at hour 0, an hour is not an int in 0–23, two modes share a start hour, or an entry is malformed.

build_water_heater(performance_map: PerformanceMap, control_schedule: list[str], control_map: dict[str, Controls], fuel_type: str = 'electric', system: str | None = 'primary') → WaterHeater[source]¶

Build a WaterHeater and add it to a heater list.

Parameters:

  • performance_map (PerformanceMap) – From build_performance_map().

  • control_schedule (list[str]) – 24-element schedule, e.g. from build_control_schedule().

  • control_map (dict[str, Controls]) – Controls for every mode in control_schedule.

  • fuel_type (str) – 'electric' or 'gas'.

  • system (str | None) – 'primary' → water_heaters, 'tm' → tm_water_heaters, 'in_series' → in_series_water_heaters, None → not added to any list (just returned).

Raises:

  • ValueError – On an unknown system or fuel_type, a schedule that is not 24 entries long, or schedule modes missing from control_map.

  • TypeError – If performance_map is not a PerformanceMap.

build_building(building_type: str, magnitude: int | float, zip_code_or_climate_zone, gpdpp: float | None = None, custom_peak_load_shape: list[float] | None = None, custom_avg_load_shape: list[float] | None = None) → Building[source]¶

Build and return a Building. The Building is not stored on the builder.

zip_code_or_climate_zone takes the same forms as in EcosizerEngine: a 5-digit CA zip string, a zone ID int, a weather station name, or a dict with 'design_oat_f' and/or 'design_inlet_water_temp_f'.

build_system(schematic: str) → DHWSystem[source]¶

Assemble the defined components into a DHWSystem.

No sizing is done and no controls are overridden: every heater runs on the control map it was built with. Heater objects are shared with the returned system, so building twice from the same builder gives two systems that share heaters.

Schematic notes¶

  • sprtp_in_parallel: exactly one primary heater must have fuel_type='gas'; it becomes the gas backup heater.

  • parallel_loop: the TM tank’s cycling temperatures are taken from the TM heater’s hour-0 controls (on_trigger_t_f / off_trigger_t_f).

  • TM and in-series slots accept one heater for now.

raises ValueError:

If the schematic is unknown, required fields are missing (all listed in one message), or heater counts are wrong.
